title: fix: return p=0 for large KS scores (green light on strongest drift) and normalise counts in PSI/JSD
body:
## Problem

`ks_prob` (`popmon/analysis/comparison/comparisons.py`) is a port of ROOT's `TMath::KolmogorovProb`, but the last branch is missing: for `z >= 6.8116` ROOT returns `0`, popmon returns `nan` (the existing test even pins `ks_prob(10.0) == nan`).

The NaN propagates to the KS z-score, and `traffic_light` puts a NaN in neither the yellow nor the red band, so the **largest drifts get a green light**.

```python
from popmon.analysis.comparison.comparisons import ks_prob
from scipy.special import kolmogorov
for z in [6.8, 6.9, 10.0, 48.0]:
    print(z, ks_prob(z), kolmogorov(z))
# 6.8   1.37e-40   1.37e-40
# 6.9   nan        8.86e-42
# 10.0  nan        2.77e-87
# 48.0  nan        0.0
```

In a full `pm_stability_report` on a normal feature, a +0.1σ shift gives a KS z-score of 5.67 (red), while a +1σ shift gives z = 48 → p = NaN → **green**.

Second issue in the same module: `population_stability_index`, `kullback_leibler_divergence` and `jensen_shannon_divergence` receive raw bin entries (counts), not proportions. Their values therefore depend on the sample sizes. For example, two weeks drawn from the same distribution give a "PSI" of 83,670; the PSI of the proportions is 0.005. The traffic light for PSI is built from deviations of the metric, so I do not claim that this changes the colour. It does change the reported number.

## Fix

- `ks_prob`: return `0` for `u >= 6.8116`, as ROOT does.
- PSI/KL/JSD: normalise the inputs to proportions before applying epsilon.

## Tests

- `test_ks_prob` now expects `0` at `z = 10`.
- New tests:
  - `test_ks_prob_large_score_is_zero_not_nan`;
  - `test_ks_zscore_large_drift_is_red`;
  - `test_psi_jsd_on_counts_equal_psi_jsd_on_proportions`.
- `tests/popmon/analysis/comparison/test_comparisons.py`: 4 failed / 5 passed before the fix, 9 passed after.
- Full suite on a local run: 25/25 in the affected test directories.

Reference values come from `scipy.special.kolmogorov` and ROOT's documented formula. I found no existing issue or PR about this, and `ks_prob` has not changed since 2020.

## Authors and AI disclosure

Reported by Xamit Kadirbekov and Daniyal Kadirbekov (GERO numerical assurance). AI tools (Claude) were used to find the case, build the reference and draft the patch and tests. The example above was re-run independently before submission.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [fix]: required update of histogrammar to patch change in numpy 2.3
body:
Update histogrammar to v1.1.1
In numpy 2.3, converting np.number to a dtype no longer allowed.

See: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/28254
"When constructing a dtype from a class with a dtype attribute, that attribute must be a dtype-instance rather than a thing that can be parsed as a dtype instance."

hist.datatype now returns float instead of np.number as datatype.

body:
-  The histograms, heatmaps and comparisons have been replaced with interactive Plotly graphs. Plotly.js is used to build the graphs on the go from json. 
- Initial tests show that plotly reports are smaller in size compared to matplotlib and the takes way less time for report generation compared to matplotlib.

comments.body:
Did you use histogrammar v1.0.28? It needs that. 
(Not sure this is right otherwise.)

Should we add this js file to our assets/ instead? 
(So there are no external dependencies.)
Already wrote it, but I think if we can switch fully to plotly, we probably should just do that.
Just remove the line.
Same as above (matplotlib dependency).

I would say either keep it this way or embed all the `JavaScript` code into the HTML file because the report would not work as a standalone HTML file if we put JS code in assets/. The drawback of adding the `CDN` source (the way Pradyot did) is that the report would not work without the internet, on the contrary, embedding this `JS` code into the `HTML` code itself would make the `HTML` code unreadable.

Actually that's what I meant: embed all the JavaScript code into the HTML file. So the report also works in an environment with limited internet access, such as DAP. We could also make a switch for this (so, make it optional) when the report is written out to file.
Agreed, I had something similar in mind regarding the optional parameter.
Yes I think that's a nice solution here.

Initially I had the js embedded in the HTML which would allow report to be visible offline but embedding it means 4MB extra file size. But it does make sense to have it available offline and doing it with parameter would be neat.

Quick wins
- Substantial part of the data  for the plotly javascript is the layout. This is the same for the plots. Reusing the same layout reduced the total file size by 50% in my experiments. Templates may be used as best practise: https://plotly.com/python/templates/#saving-and-distributing-custom-themes.
- Reports are slow to render. This can be solved by lazy loading the rendering of the plots (visible only, or one feature at a time). One example solution is using jQuery https://github.com/morr/jquery.appear, but many similar options exist. Feature-wise, we could leverage the custom-js https://github.com/ing-bank/popmon/blob/master/popmon/visualization/templates/assets/js/custom-script.js.

Improvements
- The layout above should reflect a consistent style that is readable and clear (be sure to use the same yellow/red, which differs from the default).
- The hover text for the histograms are difficult to read due to the overlay. Use unified hover mode: https://plotly.com/python/hover-text-and-formatting/#unified-hovermode
- The heatmaps have little padding. The aspect-ratio could be set to square: https://plotly.com/python/heatmaps/#controlling-aspect-ratio, and/or padding should be added
- The toolbar for the plots should be simplified by removing redundant icons :https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56659593/how-to-remove-icons-in-plotly-dash-chart-tool-bar/56659783#56659783. At least the logo and lasso tool can be removed.

Follow-up features:
- By default, the plotly express JS could be integrally included in the HTML file. The CDN option could be a new feature, as bootstrap could also be hosted by a third party. (the `online_report` option)
- Cross filter functionality would be awesome, where selecting a time-window on one plot also updates the others, e.g. https://plotly.github.io/plotly.js-crossfilter.js/
Closing in favour of https://github.com/ing-bank/popmon/pull/225

title: Refactor config
body:
## Preparations for v1.0.0 release
### Config Refactor (breaking)

Structured config using pydantic.

- Hierarchical configuration in `config.py` provides context to options
- This setup prevents code duplication (functions with many arguments, various places to set defaults, docstrings...)
- Introducing new parameters is simplified
- Documentation is updated to reflect the new syntax
- Validation is handled by the configuration, e.g. fewer type check in the code

### Profiles/Comparison Registry refactor (breaking)

The Profile and Comparison registries are extended to generalize to other existing implementations (chi2, ks, etc.)
The definitions are moved from `popmon/stats/numpy.py` to `popmon/analysis/(profiles|comparisons)`

### Enhancements
- String representation for `Pipeline` and `Module`
- Maintain section position when changing features
- Guarantee the ordering of metrics in traffic lights overview

### Removed
Removal of unused functionality:

- "worst" traffic light (unused, trivial to compute post-hoc)
- Plotting of individual alerts and traffic lights (this is replaced by the overview tables)
- docs: Removed outdated `tree`, does not provide any additional information over what's available on github

### Internal improvements / fixes
- `top` argument for plot_heatmap_b64 is now supported
- Replace `eval` with lambda functions
- Metric pipelines are now constructed of building blocks (functions) to prevent code duplication
- Make test robust against floating point error
- Enable docs api structure and jupyter notebook qa in ci/cd
